# UI Round 4 · Phase 2C Forms and Dialogs · Plan 1 (P0, primitives, ZodError fix, batch 1) Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Move the 26 batch-1 form and dialog files onto the 2A primitives, add the shared pieces they need (P0 and 2C-0), and stop raw ZodError JSON from reaching users. 2A and this plan then deploy together (spec 2A I22). Workflows, pages, data and validation behavior stay the same.

**Architecture:**
- **P0 primitives:** `Segmented`, the `Field` `labelAction` slot and the dialog trigger handles land first and reach local `master` before the rest (I1), so 2B can build on them.
- **2C-0 primitives:** the dialog parts, the translated close X, the sheet chrome, `FileDropzone`/`FileQueueList`, `Steps`/`FormSection`, `ChoiceCard`/`ChoiceChip`, `FormContextBanner` and `StickyFormFooter` sit in `src/components/ui/`, with source-text tests.
- **Guards:** one guard file, `tests/form-migration-guards.test.ts`, holds per-file budgets that start at their `5ffee76` values. Every migration task lowers its own file's budgets in the same commit, so old patterns cannot come back.
- **Server:** one change, a fixed validation message in place of `ZodError.message`.

**Tech Stack:** Next.js 16.4 App Router · Tailwind CSS 4.2.4 · class-variance-authority 0.7.1 · tailwind-merge 3.5 (through `cn()`) · radix-ui (dialog, alert-dialog) · next-intl 4 · zod · `node --test` with Node 24 type stripping.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-ui-phase2c-design.md`, with section details in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-ui-phase2c/03-primitives.md` … `09-guards-tests.md`. **Spec §10 (rulings I1–I36) overrides the section files wherever they conflict.** This plan already applies them; when a task and a section file disagree, the task wins. The 2A spec and plan (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-11-ui-phase2a-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-11-ui-phase2a.md`) define the primitives this plan builds on.

**Task numbering:** Tasks 0–22 follow spec §10.3, where task 22 is docs and wiki. This plan splits it in two: Task 22 writes the repo docs (an implementer) and Task 23 records the verify numbers and updates the wiki (the controller). Tasks 0, 21 and 23 are controller tasks. So are two steps inside implementer tasks: the master fast-forward after Task 3, and the G11b browser check in Task 18.

## Global Constraints

- **Git:**
  - Work on branch `feat/ui-phase2c`.
  - Never run `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `git rebase` or `git clean`.
  - Never touch the `master` branch: the fast-forward after Task 3 belongs to the controller (I1) and is local only, with no push.
  - Commit only the files your task names. In migration tasks, one migrated file is one commit (I30) unless the task groups files on purpose.
  - End every commit message with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
- **Next.js 16.4** is not the Next.js in your training data. Read `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before using an API you have not seen in this repo.
- **Line endings:**
  - `git config core.autocrlf` is `true`. Every batch-1 file and every `ui/` primitive this plan edits is CRLF, except:
    - `src/components/asset-operations/signature-pad.tsx` (LF)
    - `src/lib/mobile-field-navigation.ts` (mixed)
    - `src/lib/utils.ts` (LF)
  - Before you edit a file, run `git ls-files --eol <file>` and keep what it uses. Edit with exact-string replacement; never normalize a file.
  - Tests that read source files strip `\r` (`.replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")`) before multi-line regexes.
- **Tests:**
  - `npm test` runs `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` over `tests/**/*.test.{ts,mjs,js}` with Node 24 type stripping. Run one file with `node --test tests/<file>.test.ts`.
  - Modules that tests import use relative `.ts` imports (no `@/`) and erasable TypeScript only.
  - Tests cannot import `.tsx`; they check `.tsx` by reading the source text.
  - `tsconfig.json` includes `tests/`.
  - Use the shared helpers in `tests/helpers/source-files.ts` (`readSourceFiles`, `findMatches`, `countMatchesByFile`, and the JSX reader Task 7 adds).
- **Baseline before Task 1** (HEAD `a37b4d1`, whose `src/`, `tests/` and `messages/` equal `5ffee76`):
  - `npm test`: 1693 tests, 1692 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped.
  - `npx tsc --noEmit`: clean.
  - `npm run lint`: 0 errors and 146 warnings, all under `.agents/`.
  - Task 0 re-checks these numbers.
- **Every task ends with all of these green:**
  - `npm test` (0 fail)
  - `npx tsc --noEmit` (no errors)
  - `npm run lint` (0 errors, no new warnings in `src/` or `tests/`)
  - Report any failure by name.
- **Off limits:**
  - Do not run `npm ci`, `npm install`, `npm run build`, the dev server, `npx shadcn …`, or anything against a database.
  - Do not read or print `.env` or `.env.prod-admin`.
  - Leave the untracked paths alone: `.codex/`, `.impeccable/critique/`, `.playwright-mcp/`, `.superpowers/brainstorm/` and `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-22-audit-component-assets.untracked-backup.md`.
- **No new tokens (I21).** No task adds a custom property to `:root`, `@theme inline` or `@theme`, and no task edits `tests/design-tokens-contrast.test.ts`. Every class uses existing tokens and 2A primitives. Never write `rounded-[…]`.
- **Field migration rules (spec §4, §10.1):**
  - `Field label=` is the first prop.
  - `required`, `maxLength` and `minLength` stay on the control inside `Field` (K4). `Field` only adds `aria-required`, so removing the attribute would delete the only check in 18 files. Guard GF5 counts them.
  - Fields use `fieldSize` (`md` 36 · `lg` 40 · `xl` 48); default `lg`. Desktop heights of 44px become 40 (K7).
  - Phones keep ≥44px with 16px text through the 2A recipe.
  - Errors under fields stay only where they exist today: supplier ×6 (batch 2) and the asset tag/serial duplicates (Task 15).
- **No validation behavior change.**
  - Keep every existing `toast.error` guard, every `disabled` gate and every native check.
  - Field errors, focus on the first invalid field and `common.validation.*` belong to the V track, which gets its own spec after batch 1 is in Production.
  - The only behavior change in this plan is Task 8's fixed validation message.
- **Buttons (2A contract):**
  - Use `Button` / `buttonVariants`. Use `busy={x}` for work in progress and remove `x` from `disabled` on the same element (K13; guard GB).
  - A busy button keeps its label (no "กำลัง..." swaps).
  - Dialog footers use size `default` (no `size=` there; GD3).
  - `destructive` is for solid confirms; `danger` is for in-page destructive actions; the 2 audit "not found" confirms use `warning` (K22).
- **Dialogs (I6–I12):**
  - DOM order is the secondary action first and the primary last.
  - Phones stack the buttons full width (`flex-col`); from `sm` they form a right-aligned row.
  - `AccessibleDialogFooter` sits outside the scroll area.
  - No `<form>` and no `type="submit"` in the settings prefix dialog, which renders inside the settings `<form>`.
- **Messages:**
  - Edit `messages/th.json` and `messages/en.json` only through `node scripts/messages-edit.mjs <changes.json>`, run from the repo root. Keep the JSON in your temp folder.
  - Thai follows `docs/19_THAI_GLOSSARY.md` and must pass `tests/thai-glossary.test.ts`. Every key exists in both files (`tests/messages-parity.test.ts`).
  - The new keys are listed in spec §10.2.
- **Out of scope for plan 1:**
  - **2B:** list-page filters, `FilterSelect`/`ReportSelect`, list selection checkboxes (O1–O5), and the settings tab row `system-settings-form.tsx:937-956` (O7).
  - **Later batches:** batch 2–5 files, the `maintenance-attachments.tsx:239` dialog (batch 5), `AlertDialog` restyle and verb labels (batch 5), `ActionBar` (batch 5).
  - **2D:** notice boxes other than the I35 list, and form panel classes (K28).
  - **V track:** all validation UX.
- **Deploy:** plan 1 does not deploy by itself. It ships together with 2A and the other undeployed commits since `ab1b873` (spec §8.8), as one deploy that the user starts. No task in this plan deploys.

## Review Focus

1. **A user who submits a migrated form with a required field left empty** must still be stopped exactly as today (the browser's native check or the existing toast). Moving a control into `Field` must not drop `required`. Pinned by guard GF5 (the `required`/`maxLength`/`minLength` count of a migrated file never drops) in Task 7, and lowered-budget checks in every migration task.
2. **A user who presses Enter in the settings "prefix" dialog** must save only the prefix, not the whole settings form, because that dialog renders inside the settings `<form>`. Pinned by the Task 19 test (the prefix dialog has no `<form>` and no `type="submit"`). Checked with the keyboard on the dev app in Task 21.
3. **A user who clicks Save in a dialog and then tries Cancel, the X or Escape while it saves** must not close the dialog halfway. Keyboard focus must stay on the busy button. Pinned by the `AccessibleDialogCancel` busy test (Task 4) and guard GB (no `disabled={x}` next to `busy={x}`) in Task 7.
4. **Long Thai button labels in a dialog footer on a 375px phone** must stack full width and never overflow or cut. Pinned by the footer class test (`flex-col` below `sm`) in Task 4. Checked at 375 in Task 21.
5. **A user whose request fails server validation** must see a readable message, not a JSON dump. Pinned by `tests/api-error-exposure.test.ts` additions in Task 8. Checked on the dev app in Task 21 with one invalid save.

### Task 1: P0.1 `Segmented` and its two call sites

Spec §3.2 with rulings I1, I3 and I26. A new server-safe `Segmented` goes in `src/components/ui/segmented.tsx`, and the two segmented controls that 2A styled by hand move onto it: the label-name setting in `system-settings-form.tsx` (`LabelAssetNameModeField`) and the room-list tabs in `audit-scan-room-list.tsx`. One commit.

Rulings this task applies (they override `03-primitives.md` §3.2 and `08-batches.md` §8.3.1 where those differ):
- **I3:** the API and classes of §3.2:
  - `T extends string` (no boolean values) and `size` `"sm"`/`"md"`.
  - Heights are `min-h-11` with `md:min-h-8` or `md:min-h-9`. Use min-height, never `h-*`.
  - No `ring-offset` and no `trailing` option.
  - The label setting turns its boolean into `"compact"`/`"full"`.
  - The room list passes `size="md"` and `fill`, and keeps its counter as the existing `<span className="tabular-nums">` inside the option label.
  - The room-list call site is `audit-scan-room-list.tsx:72-88`. The `:81-95` in §8.3.1 is wrong.
- **I26:** the server-safe check for `segmented.tsx` goes in `tests/field-primitives.test.ts`. There is no `form-dialog-primitives.test.ts`.
- **I1 (as this plan applies it):** P0 is three tasks and three commits (Tasks 1-3).
  - They are made on `feat/ui-phase2c`, directly on top of the spec commit `a37b4d1`.
  - The controller fast-forwards local `master` after Task 3 (Task 3, Step 10).
  - The short branch `feat/ui-phase2c-p0` from I1 is skipped. `feat/ui-phase2c` already exists and holds only the spec commit above `master`. The resulting `master` is the same, plus that docs-only commit.
- **Class joining (ruled here; §3.2 is silent, §8.3.1 used a template string):**
  - The option classes are separate constants joined with `cn()`.
  - The shared part carries no `font-*`, so `font-medium` and `font-semibold` never sit in one list. That was the reason the old guard comment gave for the template string.
  - `cn()` keeps every class. Checked: `cn(shared, "md:min-h-9", "min-w-0 flex-1 px-2", pressed)` returns all of them, in order.

What users will see:
- **Settings › label print, the "asset name on the label" control:**
  - Below `md` it is 44px tall; before, it was 32px at every width. From `md` it is still 32px.
  - The focus ring loses its 2px offset.
  - The check mark still marks the chosen option, at the same 14px (`size-3.5`, which was `h-3.5 w-3.5`).
- **Audit scan room-list tabs:** the size does not change (44px, and 36px from `md`). Transitions now stop under reduced motion.

- the label (`system-settings-form.tsx:2542`, `<div className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground">{label}</div>`) and description (`:2564`) of `LabelAssetNameModeField`: batch 1f (Task 19)

File: `src/components/ui/segmented.tsx` (new)

```tsx
import * as React from "react"
import { Check } from "lucide-react"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

export type SegmentedOption<T extends string> = { value: T; label: React.ReactNode }

type SegmentedProps<T extends string> = {
  // Required: the name of the group, read before the options.
  "aria-label": string
  value: T
  options: readonly SegmentedOption<T>[]
  onValueChange: (value: T) => void
  // From md: sm is 32px (default), md is 36px. Below md both are 44px.
  size?: "sm" | "md"
  // Like the mockup's .m-seg: the frame fills its row and the options share it equally.
  fill?: boolean
  // A check mark before the chosen option's label, so the choice is not shown by color alone.
  showCheck?: boolean
  // On the frame, for layout only.
  className?: string
}

// Mockup .seg (base.css): white frame with a 1px line, 8px corners, 2px padding and gap.
const segmentedFrameClasses = "gap-0.5 rounded-md border border-border bg-surface p-0.5"
// No font weight here: the chosen option and the others bring their own, so font-medium and font-semibold never
// sit in one class list. No ring offset: the options are only 2px apart, and an offset ring would cover the neighbour.
const segmentedOptionClasses = "inline-flex min-h-11 items-center justify-center gap-1.5 rounded-control text-sm transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring"
const segmentedSizeClasses = { sm: "md:min-h-8", md: "md:min-h-9" } as const
const segmentedPressedClasses = "bg-primary-soft font-semibold text-primary-hover"
const segmentedIdleClasses = "font-medium text-muted-foreground hover:bg-background hover:text-foreground"

// A row of toggle buttons where exactly one is on (aria-pressed), each reachable with Tab (no roving tabindex, like
// the mockup). Server-safe: no directive and no hooks, like Button. onValueChange is a function, so only client
// components can render it with a handler.
function Segmented<T extends string>({
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  value,
  options,
  onValueChange,
  size = "sm",
  fill = false,
  showCheck = false,
  className,
}: SegmentedProps<T>) {
  return (
    <div role="group" aria-label={ariaLabel} data-slot="segmented" className={cn(fill ? "flex" : "inline-flex", segmentedFrameClasses, className)}>
      {options.map((option) => {
        const pressed = option.value === value
        return (
          <button
            key={option.value}
            type="button"
            aria-pressed={pressed}
            onClick={() => onValueChange(option.value)}
            className={cn(
              segmentedOptionClasses,
              segmentedSizeClasses[size],
              fill ? "min-w-0 flex-1 px-2" : "whitespace-nowrap px-3",
              pressed ? segmentedPressedClasses : segmentedIdleClasses,
            )}
          >
            {showCheck && pressed ? <Check className="size-3.5" aria-hidden="true" /> : null}
            {option.label}
          </button>
        )
      })}
    </div>
  )
}

export { Segmented }
```

Keep `const segmentedOptionClasses = "…"` on one line: the guard reads it with a one-line regex.

```js
// Task 1 check: run from the repo root after Step 6. Compiles src/app/globals.css in memory and confirms every class
// Segmented writes produces CSS (Tailwind drops a misspelled class without an error), then renders Segmented on the
// server and checks its markup. Never commit this file.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { createRequire } from "node:module"
import { resolve } from "node:path"

const require = createRequire(resolve("package.json"))
const { compile } = require("@tailwindcss/node")
const { createJiti } = require("jiti")
const React = require("react")
const { renderToStaticMarkup } = require("react-dom/server")

const compiler = await compile(readFileSync("src/app/globals.css", "utf8"), { base: resolve("src/app"), onDependency() {} })
const sources = [
  "flex inline-flex gap-0.5 rounded-md border border-border bg-surface p-0.5",
  "inline-flex min-h-11 items-center justify-center gap-1.5 rounded-control text-sm transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring",
  "md:min-h-8 md:min-h-9 min-w-0 flex-1 px-2 whitespace-nowrap px-3 size-3.5 tabular-nums",
  "bg-primary-soft font-semibold text-primary-hover",
  "font-medium text-muted-foreground hover:bg-background hover:text-foreground",
]
const classes = [...new Set(sources.flatMap((value) => value.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)))]
const css = compiler.build(classes)
const escape = (name) => name.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, (char) => `\\${char}`)
const at = (name) => css.indexOf(`.${escape(name)}`)
const missing = classes.filter((name) => at(name) === -1)
const checks = {
  [`all ${classes.length} Segmented classes compile${missing.length ? ` (missing: ${missing.join(" ")})` : ""}`]: missing.length === 0,
  "min-h-11 comes before md:min-h-8 and md:min-h-9": at("min-h-11") < at("md:min-h-8") && at("min-h-11") < at("md:min-h-9"),
}

const jiti = createJiti(resolve("package.json"), { jsx: true, alias: { "@/": `${resolve("src")}/` } })
const { Segmented } = await jiti.import(resolve("src/components/ui/segmented.tsx"))
const h = React.createElement
const setting = renderToStaticMarkup(
  h(Segmented, { "aria-label": "ชื่อทรัพย์สินในป้าย", value: "compact", options: [{ value: "compact", label: "ย่อ" }, { value: "full", label: "เต็ม" }], onValueChange() {}, showCheck: true }),
)
const rooms = renderToStaticMarkup(
  h(Segmented, { "aria-label": "สถานะรายการ", value: "checked", size: "md", fill: true, options: ["pending", "checked", "all"].map((key) => ({ value: key, label: key })), onValueChange() {} }),
)
console.log(setting)
console.log(rooms)
checks["setting: named inline group, one pressed option with a check, 32px from md"] =
  setting.startsWith('<div role="group" aria-label="ชื่อทรัพย์สินในป้าย" data-slot="segmented" class="inline-flex gap-0.5') &&
  (setting.match(/aria-pressed="true"/g) ?? []).length === 1 &&
  (setting.match(/aria-pressed="false"/g) ?? []).length === 1 &&
  setting.includes("lucide-check size-3.5") &&
  setting.includes("md:min-h-8 whitespace-nowrap px-3")
checks["room list: full-width group, 36px from md, no check mark, second option pressed"] =
  rooms.startsWith('<div role="group" aria-label="สถานะรายการ" data-slot="segmented" class="flex gap-0.5') &&
  !rooms.includes("lucide-check") &&
  (rooms.match(/md:min-h-9 min-w-0 flex-1 px-2/g) ?? []).length === 3 &&
  /aria-pressed="false"[^>]*>pending<\/button><button type="button" aria-pressed="true"/.test(rooms)

let failed = 0
for (const [name, ok] of Object.entries(checks)) {
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok   " : "WRONG"} ${name}`)
  if (!ok) failed += 1
}
if (failed) {
  console.error(`ABORT: ${failed} check(s) failed.`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log("Task 1 check passed")
```

```tsx
// The orange star after a required label, and after the text of a required <legend>. aria-hidden, because the
// control itself carries aria-required or required, so screen readers say "required" instead of "star".
```

```js
const React = require("react")
const { renderToStaticMarkup } = require("react-dom/server")

const compiler = await compile(readFileSync("src/app/globals.css", "utf8"), { base: resolve("src/app"), onDependency() {} })
const classes = [...new Set("flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5 -my-0.5 inline-flex shrink-0 text-meta font-medium text-foreground ml-1 text-warning mb-1.5 sr-only".split(" "))]

const missing = classes.filter((name) => css.indexOf(`.${escape(name)}`) === -1)

const { Field, FieldRequiredMark } = await jiti.import(resolve("src/components/ui/field.tsx"))
const { Input } = await jiti.import(resolve("src/components/ui/input.tsx"))

const withAction = renderToStaticMarkup(h(Field, { label: "สถานะ", required: true, labelAction: help }, h(Input, { id: "status" })))
const hidden = renderToStaticMarkup(h(Field, { label: "สถานะ", hideLabel: true, labelAction: help }, h(Input, { id: "status" })))
const legend = renderToStaticMarkup(h("legend", null, "ประเภทรูป", h(FieldRequiredMark)))
for (const [name, html] of Object.entries({ plain, withAction, hidden, legend })) console.log(`${name}: ${html}`)

const label = '<label data-slot="field-label" class="text-meta font-medium text-foreground" for="status">สถานะ<span aria-hidden="true" class="ml-1 text-warning">*</span></label>'
const checks = {
  [`all ${classes.length} label-row classes compile${missing.length ? ` (missing: ${missing.join(" ")})` : ""}`]: missing.length === 0,
  "without labelAction the label renders as before": plain.startsWith(`<div data-slot="field" class="grid min-w-0 gap-1.5">${label}<input`),
  "labelAction sits after </label> in one row": withAction.startsWith(
    `<div data-slot="field" class="grid min-w-0 gap-1.5"><div data-slot="field-label-row" class="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-1.5">${label}<span data-slot="field-label-action" class="-my-0.5 inline-flex shrink-0"><button`,

  "hideLabel with labelAction: sr-only label, visible button": hidden.includes('class="text-meta font-medium text-foreground sr-only"') && hidden.includes('data-slot="field-label-action"'),
  "legend star": legend === '<legend>ประเภทรูป<span aria-hidden="true" class="ml-1 text-warning">*</span></legend>',
}
let failed = 0
for (const [name, ok] of Object.entries(checks)) {
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok   " : "WRONG"} ${name}`)
  if (!ok) failed += 1
}
if (failed) {

}
console.log("Task 2 check passed")
```

```tsx
import { useId, useRef, useState, type FormEvent } from "react"
```

with

```tsx
import { useId, useImperativeHandle, useRef, useState, type FormEvent, type Ref, type RefObject } from "react"
```

The second: replace

```tsx
export function DisposalExecutionButton({
  requestId,
  disposalNo,
  disposalType,
  statuses,
  employees,
  defaultActualSaleValue,
  defaultActualSalvageValue,
  effectiveEvidenceCount,
  canUseHistoricalEvidenceException = false,
}: {
  requestId: string
  disposalNo: string
  disposalType: string
  statuses: StatusOption[]
  employees: EmployeeOption[]
  defaultActualSaleValue?: string
  defaultActualSalvageValue?: string
  effectiveEvidenceCount?: number
  canUseHistoricalEvidenceException?: boolean
}) {
```

with

```tsx
export type DisposalExecutionButtonHandle = { open: () => void }

// An owner (for example a row ⋯ menu) can render this with hideTrigger, open it through ref.current?.open() and pass
// its own button as returnFocusRef, so focus goes back there when the dialog closes.
export function DisposalExecutionButton({
  requestId,
  disposalNo,
  disposalType,
  statuses,
  employees,
  defaultActualSaleValue,
  defaultActualSalvageValue,
  effectiveEvidenceCount,
  canUseHistoricalEvidenceException = false,
  ref,
  hideTrigger = false,
  returnFocusRef,
}: {
  requestId: string
  disposalNo: string
  disposalType: string
  statuses: StatusOption[]
  employees: EmployeeOption[]
  defaultActualSaleValue?: string
  defaultActualSalvageValue?: string
  effectiveEvidenceCount?: number
  canUseHistoricalEvidenceException?: boolean
  ref?: Ref<DisposalExecutionButtonHandle>
  hideTrigger?: boolean
  returnFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
}) {
```

The third: replace

```tsx
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  const disposedStatus = statuses.find((status) => status.name === "Disposed")
```

with

```tsx
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false)
  const [saving, setSaving] = useState(false)
  useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ open: () => setOpen(true) }))
  const disposedStatus = statuses.find((status) => status.name === "Disposed")
```

The fourth (the trigger and the one-line dialog element; in the dialog line only `triggerRef={triggerRef}` changes): replace

```tsx
      <button ref={triggerRef} type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="inline-flex min-h-11 w-full items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md bg-primary px-4 text-sm font-medium text-white transition-colors hover:bg-primary-hover sm:h-10 sm:min-h-0 sm:w-auto">
        <Truck className="h-4 w-4" />
        {t("executeDisposal")}
      </button>
      {open ? <ExecutionDialog disposalNo={disposalNo} disposalType={disposalType} statuses={statuses} employees={employees} values={values} saving={saving} effectiveEvidenceCount={effectiveEvidenceCount} canUseHistoricalEvidenceException={canUseHistoricalEvidenceException} triggerRef={triggerRef} onClose={closeExecutionDialog} onSubmit={handleSubmit} onFieldChange={setField} /> : null}
```

with

```tsx
      {hideTrigger ? null : (
        <button ref={triggerRef} type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)} className="inline-flex min-h-11 w-full items-center justify-center gap-2 rounded-md bg-primary px-4 text-sm font-medium text-white transition-colors hover:bg-primary-hover sm:h-10 sm:min-h-0 sm:w-auto">
          <Truck className="h-4 w-4" />
          {t("executeDisposal")}
        </button>
      )}
      {open ? <ExecutionDialog disposalNo={disposalNo} disposalType={disposalType} statuses={statuses} employees={employees} values={values} saving={saving} effectiveEvidenceCount={effectiveEvidenceCount} canUseHistoricalEvidenceException={canUseHistoricalEvidenceException} triggerRef={returnFocusRef ?? triggerRef} onClose={closeExecutionDialog} onSubmit={handleSubmit} onFieldChange={setField} /> : null}
```

The fifth (the inner `ExecutionDialog` props type): replace

```tsx
  triggerRef: React.RefObject<HTMLButtonElement | null>
```

with

```tsx
  triggerRef: React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
```

- [ ] **Step 6: `src/components/audit/audit-mark-not-found-button.tsx`**

Four exact replacements. The first: replace

```tsx
import { useId, useState, type FormEvent } from "react"
```

with

```tsx
import { useId, useImperativeHandle, useState, type FormEvent, type Ref, type RefObject } from "react"
```

The second: replace

```tsx
export function AuditMarkNotFoundButton({ itemId, variant = "icon" }: { itemId: string; variant?: AuditMarkNotFoundButtonVariant }) {
```

with

```tsx
export type AuditMarkNotFoundButtonHandle = { open: () => void }

// An owner (for example a row ⋯ menu) can render this with hideTrigger, open it through ref.current?.open() and pass
// its own button as returnFocusRef, so focus goes back there when the dialog closes.
export function AuditMarkNotFoundButton({
  itemId,
  variant = "icon",
  ref,
  hideTrigger = false,
  returnFocusRef,
}: {
  itemId: string
  variant?: AuditMarkNotFoundButtonVariant
  ref?: Ref<AuditMarkNotFoundButtonHandle>
  hideTrigger?: boolean
  returnFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
}) {
```

The third: replace

```tsx
  function openDialog() {
    if (!saving) setDialogOpen(true)
  }
```

with

```tsx
  function openDialog() {
    if (!saving) setDialogOpen(true)
  }

  useImperativeHandle(ref, () => ({ open: openDialog }))
```

`useImperativeHandle` has no dependency list, so the handle is rebuilt every render and `open()` always sees the current `saving`.

The fourth: replace

```tsx
      {trigger}
      <AccessibleDialog
        open={dialogOpen}
        title={t("notFoundDialogTitle")}
        description={t("notFoundDialogDescription")}
        busy={saving}
        size="sm"
        onClose={closeDialog}
      >
```

with

```tsx
      {hideTrigger ? null : trigger}
      <AccessibleDialog
        open={dialogOpen}
        title={t("notFoundDialogTitle")}
        description={t("notFoundDialogDescription")}
        busy={saving}
        size="sm"
        returnFocusRef={returnFocusRef}
        onClose={closeDialog}
      >
```

`returnFocusRef` is `undefined` when no owner passes it, and then `AccessibleDialog` falls back to the element that had focus when the dialog opened, as today.

```tsx
// A real disabled attribute while busy: focus stays on the busy primary button, and the X and Escape are off as well.
export function AccessibleDialogCancel({
  children,
  disabled,
  onClick,
  ...props
}: Omit<ComponentProps<"button">, "type" | "children"> & { children?: ReactNode }) {
  const dialog = useContext(AccessibleDialogContext)
  const tCommon = useTranslations("common")
  if (!dialog) throw new Error("AccessibleDialogCancel must be used inside <AccessibleDialog>")

  return (
    <Button {...props} type="button" variant="outline" disabled={dialog.busy || disabled} onClick={onClick ?? dialog.onClose}>
      {children ?? tCommon("cancel")}
    </Button>
  )
}
```

The whole file now reads:

```tsx
"use client"

import { createContext, useContext, useRef, type ComponentProps, type ReactNode, type RefObject } from "react"
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { Dialog, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogHeader, DialogTitle } from "@/components/ui/dialog"

export type AccessibleDialogSize = "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xl"

const sizeClasses: Record<AccessibleDialogSize, string> = {
  sm: "sm:max-w-lg",
  md: "sm:max-w-2xl",
  lg: "sm:max-w-4xl",
  xl: "sm:max-w-5xl",
}

// Goes on the <form> that wraps AccessibleDialogBody and AccessibleDialogFooter. The flex column lets the body
// scroll on its own while the footer stays in view; without it the whole form scrolls and the footer can scroll away.
export const accessibleDialogFormClasses = "flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col"

// AccessibleDialogCancel reads busy and onClose from the dialog, so callers do not pass them twice.
const AccessibleDialogContext = createContext<{ busy: boolean; onClose: () => void } | null>(null)

export function AccessibleDialog({
  open,
  title,
  description,
  busy = false,
  initialFocusRef,
  returnFocusRef,
  fallbackFocusRef,
  size = "md",
  closeLabel,
  onClose,
  children,
}: {
  open: boolean
  title: string
  description?: ReactNode
  busy?: boolean
  initialFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  returnFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  fallbackFocusRef?: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>
  size?: AccessibleDialogSize
  closeLabel?: string
  onClose: () => void
  children: ReactNode
}) {
  const restoreFocusRef = useRef<HTMLElement | null>(null)

  return (
    <Dialog
      open={open}
      onOpenChange={(nextOpen) => {
        if (!nextOpen && !busy) onClose()
      }}
    >
      <DialogContent
        closeLabel={closeLabel}
        closeDisabled={busy}
        aria-busy={busy || undefined}
        {...(description ? {} : { "aria-describedby": undefined })}
        onEscapeKeyDown={(event) => {
          if (busy) event.preventDefault()
        }}
        onInteractOutside={(event) => {
          if (busy) event.preventDefault()
        }}
        onOpenAutoFocus={(event) => {
          restoreFocusRef.current = document.activeElement instanceof HTMLElement ? document.activeElement : null
          const target = initialFocusRef?.current
          if (!target) return
          event.preventDefault()
          target.focus()
        }}
        onCloseAutoFocus={(event) => {
          const target = [returnFocusRef?.current, restoreFocusRef.current, fallbackFocusRef?.current].find((candidate) => candidate?.isConnected)
          if (!target) return
          event.preventDefault()
          target.focus()
        }}
        className={cn(
          "top-auto bottom-[max(0.75rem,env(safe-area-inset-bottom))] flex max-h-[92dvh] w-[calc(100%-1.5rem)] max-w-none translate-y-0 flex-col gap-0 overflow-hidden rounded-lg border-border bg-surface p-0 shadow-overlay sm:top-[50%] sm:bottom-auto sm:translate-y-[-50%]",
          sizeClasses[size],
        )}
      >
        <DialogHeader className="shrink-0 border-b border-border px-4 py-4 pr-16 text-left sm:pl-5">
          <DialogTitle className="text-base font-semibold text-foreground">{title}</DialogTitle>
          {description ? (
            <DialogDescription className="text-sm text-muted-foreground">{description}</DialogDescription>
          ) : null}
        </DialogHeader>
        <div data-slot="accessible-dialog-content" className="flex min-h-0 flex-1 flex-col overflow-y-auto">
          <AccessibleDialogContext.Provider value={{ busy, onClose }}>{children}</AccessibleDialogContext.Provider>
        </div>
      </DialogContent>
    </Dialog>
  )
}

// The parts are optional. Children that do not use them keep their own height, so the content slot scrolls them as before.
export function AccessibleDialogBody({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<"div">) {
  return <div data-slot="accessible-dialog-body" className={cn("min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto px-4 py-4 sm:px-5", className)} {...props} />
}

// Buttons only (guard GD3), secondary first and primary last (K8): phones stack them full width with cancel on top,
// and from sm they form a right-aligned row. With no body before it, first:border-t-0 leaves the header's line alone.
export function AccessibleDialogFooter({ className, ...props }: ComponentProps<"div">) {
  return (
    <div
      data-slot="accessible-dialog-footer"
      className={cn(
        "flex shrink-0 flex-col gap-2 border-t border-border-soft bg-background px-4 py-3 first:border-t-0 sm:flex-row sm:flex-wrap sm:justify-end sm:px-5",
        className,
      )}
      {...props}
    />
  )
}

// A real disabled attribute while busy: focus stays on the busy primary button, and the X and Escape are off as well.
export function AccessibleDialogCancel({
  children,
  disabled,
  onClick,
  ...props
}: Omit<ComponentProps<"button">, "type" | "children"> & { children?: ReactNode }) {
  const dialog = useContext(AccessibleDialogContext)
  const tCommon = useTranslations("common")
  if (!dialog) throw new Error("AccessibleDialogCancel must be used inside <AccessibleDialog>")

  return (
    <Button {...props} type="button" variant="outline" disabled={dialog.busy || disabled} onClick={onClick ?? dialog.onClose}>
      {children ?? tCommon("cancel")}
    </Button>
  )
}
```

Why the 23 dialogs that do not use the parts yet keep working:
- The content slot is now a flex column that still scrolls.
- Block children keep their own height (`min-height: auto`), so the slot scrolls them as before.
- `Body` (`min-h-0 flex-1`) shrinks and scrolls by itself; `Footer` (`shrink-0`) stays at the bottom.
- A caller that forgets `accessibleDialogFormClasses` on its `<form>` gets the old behavior: the whole form scrolls. Guard GD6 (Task 7) catches that.

The status line, the new `description` line and the image hint stay inside the `<label>`, each `aria-hidden="true"` with an `id`, and the file input points at them through `aria-describedby` (a screen reader still reads text referenced that way). The field's name is the title only; inside a 2A `Field` it is "Field label + title". No `FieldHint` inside `FileDropzone`, so the three lines share one constant `subLineClasses`, and `tests/field-primitives.test.ts:131` changes (table A). `aria-invalid` (`true` or `"true"`) gives the box `"border-danger bg-surface hover:bg-background"`. `aria-required` is in the props type so a `Field` control type-checks, but it is not passed to the input.

```ts
import test from "node:test"

// Phase 2C K19 (spec 2C sections 7.6.1, 7.6.2, I13-I15). Call sites join this file in batches 1a-1e.

test("FileDropzone takes its id and aria wiring from a Field and an always-visible description", () => {
  const source = read("src/components/ui/file-dropzone.tsx")
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}hint\?: string\n/, "hint is optional: queue-mode call sites stop passing it")
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}description\?: React\.ReactNode\n/)
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}id\?: string\n/)
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}"aria-describedby"\?: string\n/)
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}"aria-invalid"\?: boolean \| "true" \| "false"\n/)
  assert.match(source, /\n {2}"aria-required"\?: boolean \| "true" \| "false"\n/)
  assert.match(source, /const inputId = id \?\? generatedId/)
  assert.match(source, /const describedBy = \[ariaDescribedBy, statusId, descriptionId, optimizeId\]\.filter\(Boolean\)\.join\(" "\)/)
  const input = source.match(/<input\n[\s\S]*?\/>/)?.[0]
  assert.ok(input, "file input not found")
  assert.match(input, /id=\{inputId\}/)
  assert.match(input, /aria-describedby=\{describedBy\}/)
  assert.match(input, /aria-invalid=\{invalid \|\| undefined\}/)
  // aria-required is accepted so Field's control props type-check, but a file input has no role that supports it.
  assert.doesNotMatch(input, /aria-required/)
})

test("FileDropzone is named by its title only; the three sub-lines are its description", () => {

  assert.equal(source.match(/aria-hidden="true" className=\{subLineClasses\}/g)?.length, 3)

  assert.match(source, /\{description \? \(\n\s+<span id=\{descriptionId\} aria-hidden="true" className=\{subLineClasses\}>\n\s+\{description\}\n/)
  assert.match(source, /<span id=\{optimizeId\} aria-hidden="true" className=\{subLineClasses\}>\n\s+\{tCommon\("imageOptimizationHint"\)\}\n/)
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Create `src/components/ui/file-queue-list.tsx`**

```tsx
"use client"

import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { X } from "lucide-react"
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl"
import { Button } from "@/components/ui/button"
import { EmptyNote } from "@/components/ui/empty-note"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

export type FileQueueItem = { id: string; name: string; detail?: ReactNode }

type FileQueueListProps = {
  items: readonly FileQueueItem[]
  onRemove: (id: string) => void
  // Name of the list. Default: common.selectedFiles; a screen reader already says how many items a list has.
  label?: string
  // Shown as an EmptyNote when nothing is queued. Without it an empty queue renders nothing.
  emptyLabel?: string
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
}

// Files picked but not uploaded yet (spec 2C section 7.6.2, I15). Taking one out deletes nothing that is saved, so
// the remove button is neutral (outline) with an X, and its name carries the file name so every row can be told apart.
export function FileQueueList({ items, onRemove, label, emptyLabel, disabled, className }: FileQueueListProps) {
  const t = useTranslations("common")

  if (items.length === 0) {
    return emptyLabel ? <EmptyNote className={className}>{emptyLabel}</EmptyNote> : null
  }

  return (
    <ul data-slot="file-queue-list" aria-label={label ?? t("selectedFiles")} className={cn("grid gap-2", className)}>
      {items.map((item) => (
        <li key={item.id} className="flex min-h-11 items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-border bg-surface py-1 pl-3 pr-1 text-sm">
          <span className="grid min-w-0 flex-1">
            <span className="truncate text-foreground">{item.name}</span>
            {item.detail ? <span className="truncate text-meta text-faint-foreground">{item.detail}</span> : null}
          </span>
          <Button
            variant="outline"
            size="icon-sm"
            disabled={disabled}
            aria-label={t("removeFile", { name: item.name })}
            onClick={() => onRemove(item.id)}
          >
            <X aria-hidden="true" />
          </Button>
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
```

```js
// Task 5 CSS check: run from the repo root. Compiles src/app/globals.css in memory and confirms every class that
// FileDropzone and FileQueueList write produces CSS. Never commit this file.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { createRequire } from "node:module"
import { resolve } from "node:path"

const require = createRequire(resolve("package.json"))
const { compile } = require("@tailwindcss/node")
const compiler = await compile(readFileSync("src/app/globals.css", "utf8"), { base: resolve("src/app"), onDependency() {} })
const sources = [
  // FileDropzone: the new invalid state and the sub-line constant
  "border-danger bg-surface hover:bg-background mt-1 block text-meta text-faint-foreground",
  // FileQueueList
  "grid gap-2 flex min-h-11 items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-border bg-surface py-1 pl-3 pr-1 text-sm min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-foreground",
]
const classes = [...new Set(sources.flatMap((value) => value.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)))]
const css = compiler.build(classes)
const escape = (name) => name.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, (char) => `\\${char}`)
const missing = classes.filter((name) => !css.includes(`.${escape(name)}`))
if (missing.length > 0) {
  console.error(`ABORT: no CSS for ${missing.join(" ")}`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`all ${classes.length} classes compile`)
```

One commit. No call site changes, except that `FormContextBanner` restyles its 5 existing sites because it is edited in place (§3.10).

Rulings this task applies (they override `03-primitives.md` §3.10–3.14 and `07-steps-choices-files.md` where they conflict):
- **I18:** the `Steps` API of §7.2: `src/lib/step-states.ts` with `getLinearStepStates(count, currentIndex, outcome = "in_progress")` and `getStepFocusIndex(states)`; `Steps({ label, steps, className })` calls `useTranslations("common")` itself and has no directive. Five flat keys: `common.stepOf` (th "ขั้นที่ {current} จาก {total}", en "Step {current} of {total}"), `stepComplete` "เสร็จแล้ว"/"Done", `stepCurrent` "ขั้นตอนปัจจุบัน"/"Current step", `stepUpcoming` "ยังไม่ถึง"/"Not started", `stepRejected` **"ปฏิเสธแล้ว"**/"Rejected" (not §7.8's "ถูกปฏิเสธ"). Label padding is `pt-px` (§7.2.2), not §3.14's `mt-px`.
- **I19:** one `FormSection` (§7.3): no `children` returns the heading row alone (`className` on the row); with `children` it returns a plain `div` (`className` on it) with the row (`mb-4`) above the body. No `FormSectionHeader`, no `<section aria-labelledby>`.
- **I20:** §7.4 is the base (input always visible, `"use client"`, `preventEnterSubmit`, prop `detail`) with the disabled rule of §3.13: a disabled choice that is chosen keeps its `primary-soft` fill (`has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:…`). The two `<label>` class strings, the input classes and the description classes are I20 verbatim.
- **I21:** P1 (bulk move rows) and P3 (`aria-pressed` on candidate rows) are not `ChoiceCard`; they are batch work (1b, 1e). This task only exports `preventEnterSubmit` for P1.
- **I26:** the server-safe rule applies to `steps.tsx` (it may call `useTranslations`), `form-section.tsx` and `form-context-banner.tsx`, not to `choice-card.tsx`. The `FormContextBanner` test goes in `tests/field-primitives.test.ts` (§9.6).
- **Plan rulings (spec gaps):**
  - **GF2 (Task 7) and `<input type={type}>`:** §7.4.1 passes `type` to one `<input>`. Task 7's GF2 counts every `<input>` whose `type` is not literally `checkbox`, `radio`, `hidden` or `file` as a hand-written text field, and `ui/choice-card.tsx` is in `NEW_2C_FILES` with budget 0, so that markup would fail GF2 on day one. `choice-card.tsx` therefore renders the input through a private `NativeChoice` that writes `<input type="radio" …/>` or `<input type="checkbox" …/>`. The DOM is the same as §7.4.1: one browser input inside the `<label>`. Task 7 needs no exception.
  - `getLinearStepStates`: a count of 0 or less gives `[]`; a non-finite index counts as 0; a fractional index is truncated (then clamped as §7.2.1 says).
  - `Steps` renders nothing for an empty list. The phone line uses the focus step's own label class, as §7.2.2 writes it (§3.14 made it always `font-semibold text-foreground`).
  - `ChoiceCard`/`ChoiceChip` name the input with `aria-labelledby` on the label span and add the description or detail to the caller's own `aria-describedby`; a caller's `aria-labelledby` is replaced.
  - `FormContextBanner` gets `data-slot="form-context-banner"` (shared rule of §3.1: every primitive has a `data-slot`).

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict"
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import test from "node:test"
import { cn } from "../src/lib/utils.ts"

// Phase 2C K16 (spec 2C section 7.4, I20, I21). Call sites join this file in 1a, 1b, 1c, 1e, 1f and batch 4.
const read = (path: string) => readFileSync(path, "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")
const choice = () => read("src/components/ui/choice-card.tsx")

// Spec I20, verbatim. Tailwind emits hover:, has-checked:, has-disabled:, has-[…]: in that order, so a chosen card keeps
// its primary border on hover, and only a disabled choice that is not chosen loses its fill.
const CARD =
  "group flex min-h-11 cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-md border border-control-border bg-surface px-3 py-2.5 text-sm text-foreground transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none hover:border-input has-checked:border-primary has-checked:bg-primary-soft has-disabled:cursor-not-allowed has-disabled:text-faint-foreground has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:border-border has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:bg-background"
const CHIP =
  "inline-flex min-h-11 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 rounded-control border border-control-border bg-surface px-3 py-1 text-sm text-foreground transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none hover:border-input md:min-h-8 has-checked:border-primary-border has-checked:bg-primary-soft has-checked:text-primary-hover has-disabled:cursor-not-allowed has-disabled:text-faint-foreground has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:border-border has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:bg-background"

test("ChoiceCard and ChoiceChip draw on a real, visible input inside a label, styled with has-checked", () => {
  const source = choice()
  assert.match(source, /^"use client"\n/, "the Enter guard is an event handler")
  assert.ok(source.includes(`const choiceCardClasses =\n  "${CARD}"`), "ChoiceCard label classes (I20)")
  assert.ok(source.includes(`const choiceChipClasses =\n  "${CHIP}"`), "ChoiceChip label classes (I20)")
  assert.match(source, /<label data-slot="choice-card" className=\{cn\(choiceCardClasses, className\)\}>/)
  assert.match(source, /<label data-slot="choice-chip" className=\{cn\(choiceChipClasses, className\)\}>/)
  assert.match(source, /className=\{cn\(checkboxVariants\(\), "mt-0\.5"\)\}/)
  assert.match(source, /className=\{checkboxVariants\(\)\}/)
  assert.match(source, /className="text-meta text-muted-foreground group-has-disabled:text-faint-foreground"/)
  assert.match(source, /className="text-meta text-faint-foreground"/)
  // accent-color and the base :focus-visible outline already style the input; hiding the input would cut its outline off.
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /accent-primary|focus-within:ring|sr-only|opacity-|shadow-|leading-tight|rounded-\[/)
  // Literal types: the form-migration guard GF2 counts an <input> whose type is not checkbox, radio, hidden or file.
  assert.match(source, /type === "radio" \? <input type="radio" \{\.\.\.props\} onKeyDown=\{handleKeyDown\} \/> : <input type="checkbox" \{\.\.\.props\} onKeyDown=\{handleKeyDown\} \/>/)
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /<input\b(?![^>]*\btype="(?:radio|checkbox)")/)
})

test("cn() keeps every class of the two choice recipes", () => {
  for (const recipe of [CARD, CHIP]) assert.equal(cn(recipe), recipe)
})

test("Enter on a choice never submits the form, and the caller's onKeyDown runs first", () => {
  const source = choice()
  assert.match(source, /export function preventEnterSubmit\(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>\) \{\n {2}if \(event\.key === "Enter"\) event\.preventDefault\(\)\n\}/)
  assert.match(source, /function handleKeyDown\(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>\) \{\n\s+onKeyDown\?\.\(event\)\n\s+preventEnterSubmit\(event\)\n\s+\}/)
})

test("a choice is named by its label and described by its description or detail", () => {
  const source = choice()
  assert.match(source, /const describedBy = \[ariaDescribedBy, extraId\]\.filter\(Boolean\)\.join\(" "\) \|\| undefined/)
  // The caller's input props go first, so they cannot replace the type or the ids.
  assert.equal(source.match(/<NativeChoice\n\s+\{\.\.\.inputProps\}\n\s+type=\{type\}\n\s+aria-labelledby=\{labelId\}\n\s+aria-describedby=\{describedBy\}/g)?.length, 2)
  assert.match(source, /<span id=\{labelId\} className="font-medium">/)
  assert.match(source, /<span id=\{labelId\}>\{label\}<\/span>/)
})
```

- [ ] **Step 8: Create `src/lib/step-states.ts`**

```ts
// States for the Steps rail (src/components/ui/steps.tsx, spec 2C section 7.2.1). Plain TS with no React and no
// "@/" imports, so tests import this file directly.
export type StepState = "complete" | "current" | "upcoming" | "rejected"
export type StepOutcome = "in_progress" | "complete" | "rejected"

// Steps before currentIndex are complete, the one at currentIndex is current (or rejected), the rest are upcoming.
// A complete flow has every step complete and none current. currentIndex is pulled into 0 … count - 1, so an
// indexOf() miss (-1) points at the first step.
export function getLinearStepStates(count: number, currentIndex: number, outcome: StepOutcome = "in_progress"): StepState[] {
  if (count <= 0) return []
  if (outcome === "complete") return Array.from({ length: count }, (): StepState => "complete")
  const index = Number.isFinite(currentIndex) ? Math.trunc(currentIndex) : 0
  const current = Math.min(Math.max(index, 0), count - 1)
  const marker: StepState = outcome === "rejected" ? "rejected" : "current"
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, step): StepState => (step < current ? "complete" : step === current ? marker : "upcoming"))
}

// The step the phone line names: the current or rejected step, else the last step once all are complete, else the first.
export function getStepFocusIndex(states: readonly StepState[]): number {
  const active = states.findIndex((state) => state === "current" || state === "rejected")
  if (active !== -1) return active
  if (states.length > 0 && states.every((state) => state === "complete")) return states.length - 1
  return 0
}
```

- [ ] **Step 9: Create `src/components/ui/steps.tsx`**

```tsx
import { Check, X } from "lucide-react"
import { useTranslations } from "next-intl"
import { getStepFocusIndex, type StepState } from "@/lib/step-states"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

export type StepItem = { id: string; label: string; state: StepState }

// Marker rail (spec 2C section 7.2, K17): 22px circles joined by a line. The state shows by shape (number, check, X)
// and by a hidden word, never by color alone. Each state is its own string: a status soft fill never shares a class
// string with faint text. No frame of its own; place it in a panel with a margin class.
const markerBase = "inline-flex size-5.5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border text-xs font-semibold num"
const markerByState: Record<StepState, string> = {
  complete: "border-success-border bg-success-soft text-success",
  current: "border-primary bg-primary-soft text-primary-hover",
  upcoming: "border-control-border bg-surface text-faint-foreground",
  rejected: "border-danger-border bg-danger-soft text-danger",
}
const labelByState: Record<StepState, string> = {
  complete: "text-muted-foreground",
  current: "font-semibold text-foreground",
  upcoming: "text-faint-foreground",
  rejected: "font-medium text-danger",
}
const stateWordKeys: Record<StepState, string> = {
  complete: "stepComplete",
  current: "stepCurrent",
  upcoming: "stepUpcoming",
  rejected: "stepRejected",
}

// No client directive: useTranslations is the only hook, so server pages (the disposal request) render it too.
// Below md every label is sr-only and one aria-hidden line names the focus step; the list already reads every step.
export function Steps({ label, steps, className }: { label: string; steps: readonly StepItem[]; className?: string }) {
  const t = useTranslations("common")
  if (steps.length === 0) return null
  const focus = getStepFocusIndex(steps.map((step) => step.state))
  const focusStep = steps[focus]

  return (
    <div data-slot="steps" className={className}>
      <ol aria-label={label} className="flex items-start gap-2">
        {steps.map((step, index) => (
          <li
            key={step.id}
            aria-current={step.state === "current" ? "step" : undefined}
            className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-start gap-2 last:flex-none"
          >
            <span aria-hidden="true" className={cn(markerBase, markerByState[step.state])}>
              {step.state === "complete" ? (
                <Check className="size-3.5" strokeWidth={2.75} />
              ) : step.state === "rejected" ? (
                <X className="size-3.5" strokeWidth={2.75} />
              ) : index + 1}
            </span>
            <span className={cn("min-w-0 pt-px text-meta max-md:sr-only", labelByState[step.state])}>
              <span className="sr-only">{t(stateWordKeys[step.state])}: </span>
              {step.label}
            </span>
            {index < steps.length - 1 ? (
              <span aria-hidden="true" className={cn("mt-2.75 h-px min-w-3 flex-1", step.state === "complete" ? "bg-success-border" : "bg-border")} />
            ) : null}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ol>
      <p aria-hidden="true" className="mt-2 text-meta text-faint-foreground md:hidden">
        <span className="num">{t("stepOf", { current: focus + 1, total: steps.length })}</span> · <span className={labelByState[focusStep.state]}>{focusStep.label}</span>
      </p>
    </div>
  )
}
```

Why these numbers (spec §7.2.2–7.2.3): `size-5.5` is the mockup's 22px `.check .mark`; `mt-2.75` (11px) puts the 1px connector on the marker's middle line; `pt-px` centers the 20px `text-meta` line on the 22px marker. Below `md` the labels are `sr-only` (absolute, so they take no room) and 5 steps need 5 × 22 + 4 × (8 + 12) + 4 × 8 = 222px of the 283px inside a 375px screen.

- [ ] **Step 10: Create `src/components/ui/form-section.tsx`**

```tsx
import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

type FormSectionProps = {
  number?: number
  title: ReactNode
  // h3 under a page that already has an h2 section title (the settings page).
  as?: "h2" | "h3"
  className?: string
  children?: ReactNode
}

const headingClasses = {
  h2: "text-base font-semibold text-foreground",
  h3: "text-sm font-semibold text-foreground",
}

// A numbered form section heading (spec 2C section 7.3, K18). The number is decoration in a quiet outlined circle,
// never the filled "current step" look; Steps is the only progress indicator. Without children it returns the heading
// row alone, for forms that place it as one row of a grid (className goes on the row). With children it wraps them in
// a plain div, not a section element, so a long settings page does not get one landmark region per section. Server-safe.
export function FormSection({ number, title, as: Heading = "h2", className, children }: FormSectionProps) {
  const hasBody = children !== undefined && children !== null
  const heading = (
    <div data-slot="form-section-heading" className={cn("flex items-center gap-2.5 border-b border-border-soft pb-2.5", hasBody ? "mb-4" : className)}>
      {number !== undefined ? (
        <span
          aria-hidden="true"
          className="inline-flex size-5.5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border border-control-border text-xs font-semibold text-muted-foreground num"
        >
          {number}
        </span>
      ) : null}
      <Heading className={headingClasses[Heading]}>{title}</Heading>
    </div>
  )

  if (!hasBody) return heading

  return (
    <div data-slot="form-section" className={className}>
      {heading}
      {children}
    </div>
  )
}
```

- [ ] **Step 11: Create `src/components/ui/choice-card.tsx`**

```tsx
"use client"

import { useId, type ComponentProps, type KeyboardEvent, type ReactNode } from "react"
import { checkboxVariants } from "@/components/ui/field-variants"
import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

// Radio and checkbox choices drawn on the browser's own input inside a <label> (spec 2C section 7.4, I20). The input
// stays visible, so a choice never shows by color alone, browsers without :has() still show the state, and the focus
// outline comes from the input itself. className goes on the <label> and is for layout only.
type ChoiceInputProps = Omit<ComponentProps<"input">, "type" | "size" | "className" | "children">

type ChoiceBaseProps = ChoiceInputProps & {
  type: "radio" | "checkbox"
  label: ReactNode
  className?: string
}

// Tailwind emits hover:, has-checked:, has-disabled:, has-[…]: in that order: a chosen choice keeps its primary border on
// hover, and only a disabled choice that is not chosen loses its fill (a disabled chosen one keeps primary-soft).
const choiceCardClasses =
  "group flex min-h-11 cursor-pointer items-start gap-3 rounded-md border border-control-border bg-surface px-3 py-2.5 text-sm text-foreground transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none hover:border-input has-checked:border-primary has-checked:bg-primary-soft has-disabled:cursor-not-allowed has-disabled:text-faint-foreground has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:border-border has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:bg-background"
const choiceChipClasses =
  "inline-flex min-h-11 cursor-pointer items-center gap-2 rounded-control border border-control-border bg-surface px-3 py-1 text-sm text-foreground transition-colors motion-reduce:transition-none hover:border-input md:min-h-8 has-checked:border-primary-border has-checked:bg-primary-soft has-checked:text-primary-hover has-disabled:cursor-not-allowed has-disabled:text-faint-foreground has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:border-border has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:bg-background"

// Chromium submits the form when Enter is pressed on a checkbox or radio (implicit submission). These choices replace
// type="button" toggles inside the settings and asset forms, so Enter must not save the whole form. Space still toggles.
export function preventEnterSubmit(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
  if (event.key === "Enter") event.preventDefault()
}

// The native input. Each tag has a literal type, so the form-migration guards read it as a choice, not as a
// hand-written text field. The caller's onKeyDown runs first, then the Enter guard.
function NativeChoice({ type, onKeyDown, ...props }: ChoiceInputProps & { type: "radio" | "checkbox"; className: string }) {
  function handleKeyDown(event: KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) {
    onKeyDown?.(event)
    preventEnterSubmit(event)
  }

  return type === "radio" ? <input type="radio" {...props} onKeyDown={handleKeyDown} /> : <input type="checkbox" {...props} onKeyDown={handleKeyDown} />
}

// The input is named by the label text only; the description or detail is read after it, as its description.
function useChoiceIds(extra: ReactNode, ariaDescribedBy: string | undefined) {
  const id = useId()
  const labelId = `${id}-label`
  const extraId = extra ? `${id}-extra` : undefined
  const describedBy = [ariaDescribedBy, extraId].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || undefined
  return { labelId, extraId, describedBy }
}

// A full-width option card (8px corners): handover mode, repair outcome.
export function ChoiceCard({
  type,
  label,
  description,
  className,
  "aria-describedby": ariaDescribedBy,
  ...inputProps
}: ChoiceBaseProps & { description?: ReactNode }) {
  const { labelId, extraId, describedBy } = useChoiceIds(description, ariaDescribedBy)

  return (
    <label data-slot="choice-card" className={cn(choiceCardClasses, className)}>
      <NativeChoice
        {...inputProps}
        type={type}
        aria-labelledby={labelId}
        aria-describedby={describedBy}
        className={cn(checkboxVariants(), "mt-0.5")}
      />
      <span className="grid min-w-0 gap-0.5">
        <span id={labelId} className="font-medium">
          {label}
        </span>
        {description ? (
          <span id={extraId} className="text-meta text-muted-foreground group-has-disabled:text-faint-foreground">
            {description}
          </span>
        ) : null}
      </span>
    </label>
  )
}

// A small inline option (6px corners, 32px from md like a sm button): optional columns, photo type, depreciation group.
export function ChoiceChip({
  type,
  label,
  detail,
  className,
  "aria-describedby": ariaDescribedBy,
  ...inputProps
}: ChoiceBaseProps & { detail?: ReactNode }) {
  const { labelId, extraId, describedBy } = useChoiceIds(detail, ariaDescribedBy)

  return (
    <label data-slot="choice-chip" className={cn(choiceChipClasses, className)}>
      <NativeChoice
        {...inputProps}
        type={type}
        aria-labelledby={labelId}
        aria-describedby={describedBy}
        className={checkboxVariants()}
      />
      <span id={labelId}>{label}</span>
      {detail ? (
        <span id={extraId} className="text-meta text-faint-foreground">
          {detail}
        </span>
      ) : null}
    </label>
  )
}
```

Notes:
- `NativeChoice` is the plan ruling above (GF2): one browser input with a literal `type`, so the rendered DOM is the §7.4.1 markup.
- The caller's props are spread first, so `type`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `onKeyDown` and `className` cannot be overridden. `onKeyDown` runs the caller's handler, then `preventEnterSubmit`. Space still toggles; Enter on R1–R3 no longer submits (§7.4.2, the behavior change of §7.14 risk 1).
- No `accent-primary` (`:root` sets `accent-color`), no `focus-within:ring` (the input's own `:focus-visible` outline shows), no `sr-only` on the input (it would cut the outline off).

```js
// Task 6 CSS check: run from the repo root. Compiles src/app/globals.css in memory and confirms every class of the
// choice, step, section and banner primitives produces CSS, and that the state rules land after the ones they beat.
// Never commit this file.
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { createRequire } from "node:module"
import { resolve } from "node:path"

const require = createRequire(resolve("package.json"))
const { compile } = require("@tailwindcss/node")
const compiler = await compile(readFileSync("src/app/globals.css", "utf8"), { base: resolve("src/app"), onDependency() {} })
const choiceCard = readFileSync("src/components/ui/choice-card.tsx", "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")
const recipe = (name) => choiceCard.match(new RegExp(`const ${name} =\n  "([^"]+)"`))?.[1] ?? ""
const sources = [
  recipe("choiceCardClasses"),
  recipe("choiceChipClasses"),
  "mt-0.5 grid min-w-0 gap-0.5 font-medium text-meta text-muted-foreground group-has-disabled:text-faint-foreground text-faint-foreground",
  // Steps
  "inline-flex size-5.5 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-full border text-xs font-semibold num",
  "border-success-border bg-success-soft text-success border-primary bg-primary-soft text-primary-hover border-control-border bg-surface text-faint-foreground border-danger-border bg-danger-soft text-danger",
  "text-muted-foreground font-semibold text-foreground font-medium flex items-start gap-2 min-w-0 flex-1 last:flex-none size-3.5",
  "pt-px text-meta max-md:sr-only sr-only mt-2.75 h-px min-w-3 bg-success-border bg-border mt-2 md:hidden",
  // FormSection
  "flex items-center gap-2.5 border-b border-border-soft pb-2.5 mb-4 text-base text-sm",
  // FormContextBanner
  "flex-wrap items-baseline gap-x-3 gap-y-0.5 break-words tag",
]
if (!sources[0] || !sources[1]) {
  console.error("ABORT: choiceCardClasses or choiceChipClasses not found")
  process.exit(1)
}
const classes = [...new Set(sources.flatMap((value) => value.split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean)))].filter((name) => name !== "group")
const css = compiler.build(classes)
const escape = (name) => name.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, (char) => `\\${char}`)
const at = (name) => css.indexOf(`.${escape(name)}`)
const missing = classes.filter((name) => at(name) === -1)
let failures = missing.length
if (missing.length > 0) console.error("MISSING CSS:", missing.join(" "))
for (const [before, after] of [
  ["hover:border-input", "has-checked:border-primary"],
  ["has-checked:border-primary-border", "has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:border-border"],
  ["has-checked:bg-primary-soft", "has-[:disabled:not(:checked)]:bg-background"],
  ["has-checked:text-primary-hover", "has-disabled:text-faint-foreground"],
  ["min-h-11", "md:min-h-8"],
  ["text-muted-foreground", "group-has-disabled:text-faint-foreground"],
]) {
  const ok = at(before) !== -1 && at(before) < at(after)
  if (!ok) failures += 1
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok   " : "WRONG"} ${before} before ${after}`)
}
if (failures > 0) {
  console.error(`ABORT: ${failures} problem(s). A class name is misspelled or its token is missing.`)
  process.exit(1)
}
console.log(`all ${classes.length} classes compile`)
```

```ts
import assert from "node:assert/strict"
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs"
import test from "node:test"

const footer = () => readFileSync("src/components/ui/sticky-form-footer.tsx", "utf8").replace(/\r\n/g, "\n")

test("StickyFormFooter is a server-safe save bar that sticks to the bottom of the scroll area (K14, I22)", () => {
  const source = footer()
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /"use client"|\buse(?:State|Effect|LayoutEffect|Ref|Context|Id)\b|createContext/, "no directive and no hook: server pages may render it")
  assert.match(source, /type StickyFormFooterProps = React\.ComponentProps<"div"> & \{\s*\/\*\*[^*]*\*\/\s*status\?: React\.ReactNode\s*\}/)
  assert.match(source, /export function StickyFormFooter\(\{ status, className, children, \.\.\.props \}: StickyFormFooterProps\)/)
  assert.match(source, /data-slot="sticky-form-footer"/)
  // -bottom-4 sm:-bottom-6 and -mx-4 sm:-mx-6 cancel the padding of main (layout/dashboard-shell.tsx), as the audit scan search does with -top-4 sm:-top-6.
  assert.match(
    source,
    /cn\(\s*"sticky -bottom-4 z-10 -mx-4 border-t border-border bg-canvas px-4 pt-3 pb-\[max\(0\.75rem,env\(safe-area-inset-bottom\)\)\] sm:-bottom-6 sm:-mx-6 sm:px-6",\s*className,\s*\)/,
  )
  assert.match(source, /\{\.\.\.props\}/)
  assert.match(source, /<div className="flex flex-col gap-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center">/)
  assert.match(source, /\{status \? <div className="min-w-0 flex-1 text-meta text-muted-foreground">\{status\}<\/div> : null\}/)
  assert.match(source, /<div className="flex flex-col gap-2 sm:ml-auto sm:flex-row sm:flex-wrap sm:items-center sm:justify-end">\{children\}<\/div>/)
})

test("StickyFormFooter is flat, keeps the DOM button order and blends into the canvas", () => {
  const source = footer()
  // Full-bleed sticky bars use the canvas fill (DESIGN.md §2, visual-foundation-guards "full-bleed bars blend into the canvas").
  assert.doesNotMatch(source, /\bbg-surface\b|\bshadow-|\bfixed\b|backdrop-blur|\brounded-|flex-col-reverse/)
})
```

```ts
// Same message as assertWithinBudget in visual-foundation-guards.test.ts, but over counts taken already (so a JSX count works too).
function assertWithinBudget(counts: Record<string, number>, budget: Record<string, number>, what: string) {
  const total = Object.values(counts).reduce((sum, count) => sum + count, 0)
  assert.deepEqual(
    budgetOverruns(counts, budget),
    [],
    `${what}: ${total} in ${Object.keys(counts).length} files. Lower a number in the task that removes a site; never raise one. Phase 2D widens every guard to all of src and sets the budgets to {}.`,
  )
}

test("the JSX reader skips arrows, selectors, braces, quoted text and comments", () => {
  const source = [
    '<input onChange={(e) => set(e.target.value)} className="[&>svg]:size-4 required" required />',
    '<Field label={t("a")} required>',
    '  <Input value={x > 1 ? "a" : "b"} maxLength={20} />',
    "</Field>",
    "// <input commented />",
    '<label htmlFor="n"><label>inner</label></label>',
    '<Field label={t("open")}>',
  ].join("\n")
  const [input, ...more] = findJsxTags(source, ["input"])
  assert.equal(more.length, 0, "a tag on a // line is a comment")
  assert.equal(hasJsxAttr(input.text, "required"), true)
  assert.equal(input.selfClosing, true)
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(input.text, "className"), "[&>svg]:size-4 required")
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(input.text, "onChange"), "(e) => set(e.target.value)")
  const [field, open] = findJsxElements(source, "Field")
  assert.equal(field.line, 2)
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(field.text, "label"), 't("a")')
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(field.text, "required"), "")
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(field.text, "hint"), null)
  assert.match(field.children ?? "", /<Input value=/)
  assert.equal(open.children, null, "no closing tag")
  const [control] = findJsxTags(field.children ?? "", ["Input"])
  assert.equal(jsxAttrValue(control.text, "maxLength"), "20")
  const [outer] = findJsxElements(source, "label")
  assert.equal(outer.children, "<label>inner</label>", "same-name nesting is counted")
  assert.equal(hasJsxAttr("<Input value={required} />", "required"), false)
  assert.equal(hasJsxAttr('<Input className="x required" />', "required"), false)
  assert.equal(hasJsxAttr("<Input aria-required />", "required"), false)
  assert.equal(findJsxTags("<SelectField required />", ["Select"]).length, 0)
  assert.deepEqual(countByFile([{ path: "src/a.tsx", source: "<input /><input />" }, { path: "src/b.tsx", source: "" }], (file) => findJsxTags(file.source, ["input"]).length), { "src/a.tsx": 2 })
  assert.deepEqual(budgetOverruns({ "src/a.tsx": 2, "src/b.tsx": 1 }, { "src/a.tsx": 2 }), ["src/b.tsx: 1 > 0"])
})

test("the guard's own lists name real 2C files", () => {
  const exists = (path: string) => sources.some((file) => file.path === path)
  const problems: string[] = []
  for (const path of Object.values(BATCH_FILES).flat()) if (!exists(C + path)) problems.push(`BATCH_FILES: ${path} not found`)
  for (const path of MIGRATED_FILES) if (!owned.has(path)) problems.push(`MIGRATED_FILES: ${path} is not a 2C file`)
  const ownedKeys = {
    LOCAL_FIELD,
    RAW_FIELDS,
    FIELD_CLASS_STRINGS,
    CONSTRAINT_FLOORS,
    OLD_MARKUP,
    LOADER2,
    OLD_HELPERS,
    CLOSE_LABEL_IS_CANCEL,
    FIXED_BOTTOM_BARS,
    BUSY_LABEL_SWAPS,
    STICKY_FOOTER_ROUTES,
  }
  for (const [name, budget] of Object.entries(ownedKeys)) {
    for (const path of Object.keys(budget)) if (!owned.has(path)) problems.push(`${name}: ${path} is not a 2C file`)
  }
  for (const path of Object.keys(REVERSE)) if (!owned.has(path) && !path.startsWith(`${C}ui/`)) problems.push(`REVERSE: ${path} is outside the 2C files and ui/`)
  for (const path of PENDING_FOOTER_PARTS) if (!owned.has(path)) problems.push(`PENDING_FOOTER_PARTS: ${path} is not a 2C file`)
  assert.deepEqual(problems, [])
})

test("GF4 a Field that shows the required star keeps native required on its control (critic risk 5)", () => {
  const problems: string[] = []
  for (const file of migratedSources()) {
    const vTrack = /\bnoValidate\b/.test(file.source) && /\bvalidate\(/.test(file.source)
    for (const field of findJsxElements(file.source, "Field")) {
      const where = `${file.path}:${field.line}`
      const children = field.children ?? ""
      if (findJsxTags(children, ["SearchableSelect"]).length > 0) problems.push(`${where}: SearchableSelect inside Field (it renders its own label)`)
      // The first control (a file input counts; checkbox, radio and hidden do not).
      const control = findJsxTags(children, CONTROL_TAGS).find((tag) => !/^(?:checkbox|radio|hidden)$/.test(jsxAttrValue(tag.text, "type") ?? ""))
      const star = hasJsxAttr(field.text, "required")
      const native = control ? hasJsxAttr(control.text, "required") : /\brequired\b/.test(children)
      const exempt = STAR_ONLY.has(`${file.path}|${jsxAttrValue(field.text, "label")}`)
      if (star && !native && !vTrack && !exempt) problems.push(`${where}: star without native required (the only browser check would disappear)`)
      if (native && !star) problems.push(`${where}: native required without the star`)
    }
  }
  assert.deepEqual(problems, [])
})

test("GF5 required, maxLength and minLength never disappear quietly (K4)", () => {
  const lost: string[] = []
  for (const [path, floor] of Object.entries(CONSTRAINT_FLOORS)) {
    const tags = findJsxTags(read(path), CONSTRAINT_TAGS)
    CONSTRAINT_ATTRS.forEach((attr, index) => {
      const count = tags.filter((tag) => hasJsxAttr(tag.text, attr)).length
      if (count < floor[index]) lost.push(`${path}: ${attr} ${count} < ${floor[index]}`)
    })
  }
  assert.deepEqual(lost, [], "Field only adds aria-required: keep required, maxLength and minLength on the control itself")
})

test("GB2 a spinner outside a button stops for users who reduce motion", () => {
  const problems: string[] = []
  for (const file of migratedSources()) {
    const buttons = [...findJsxElements(file.source, "Button"), ...findJsxElements(file.source, "button")].filter((button) => button.children !== null)
    for (const loader of findJsxTags(file.source, ["Loader2"])) {
      const inButton = buttons.some((button) => loader.start >= button.end && loader.start < button.closeEnd)
      if (!inButton && !/\bmotion-reduce:animate-none\b/.test(loader.text)) problems.push(`${file.path}:${loader.line}`)
    }
  }
  assert.deepEqual(problems, [], "add motion-reduce:animate-none")
})

test("GB4 disabled never repeats the busy condition, so focus stays on the busy button", () => {
  const problems: string[] = []
  let busyTags = 0
  for (const file of sources) {
    for (const tag of findJsxTags(file.source, ["[A-Za-z][\\w.]*"])) {
      const busy = jsxAttrValue(tag.text, "busy")
      if (busy === null) continue
      busyTags++
      const disabled = jsxAttrValue(tag.text, "disabled")
      if (disabled === null || busy.trim() === "") continue
      const expression = busy.trim().replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, "\\$&").replace(/\s+/g, "\\s*")
      if (new RegExp(`(?<![\\w.$])${expression}(?![\\w$])`).test(disabled)) problems.push(`${file.path}:${tag.line}: busy={${busy}} disabled={${disabled}}`)
    }
  }
  assert.ok(busyTags > 0, "the reader found no busy= at all")
  assert.deepEqual(problems, [])
})

test("GD1 close buttons are named in the reader's language, never Close or Cancel", () => {

    .filter((path) => !read(path) || /"Close"|>\s*Close\s*</.test(read(path)))
  assert.deepEqual(english, [], 'these dialog primitives are missing or still say "Close"')
  assert.deepEqual(findMatches(sources, LITERAL_CLOSE_LABEL), [], 'take the X label from tCommon("close") or a key')
  assertWithinBudget(countMatchesByFile(sources, CLOSE_IS_CANCEL), CLOSE_LABEL_IS_CANCEL, "GD1 closeLabel set to a cancel label")
})

test("GD2 migrated dialogs use the footer part, and the pending list holds only files still waiting", () => {
  const problems: string[] = []
  for (const file of sources) {
    if (file.path === `${C}ui/accessible-dialog.tsx`) continue
    const dialogs = findJsxTags(file.source, ["AccessibleDialog"]).length
    const footers = findJsxTags(file.source, ["AccessibleDialogFooter"]).length
    if (PENDING_FOOTER_PARTS.has(file.path)) {
      if (dialogs === 0) problems.push(`${file.path}: no AccessibleDialog left; remove it from PENDING_FOOTER_PARTS`)
      if (footers > 0) problems.push(`${file.path}: uses AccessibleDialogFooter now; remove it from PENDING_FOOTER_PARTS`)
    } else if (footers < dialogs) problems.push(`${file.path}: ${dialogs} AccessibleDialog, ${footers} AccessibleDialogFooter`)
  }
```
